@nextcloud/vue: 1,662,797 B in 247 modules, 45.4 % of the static path of bookmarks-main.js, imported by its root in 31 files: admin.js (Tooltip), components/Bookmark.vue (NcActionButton, NcActionCheckbox, NcPopover), and 29 more. It is imported per module as well, through 1 other specifier.
Importing the module that is used instead of the package root lets the bundler drop the rest of the barrel.
ncmake's lint-vue-imports workflow gates exactly this specifier for @nextcloud/vue, so this finding is that red check with a byte figure attached.

45 components of @nextcloud/vue are delivered although no file in src names them, no other dependency names them and no component named by either imports them: 99,541 B, 2.7 % of the static path of bookmarks-main.js, next to 33 components the source names, 1 that other dependencies name and 22 those pull in.

These arrive through the root import: under a barrel the whole component set is reachable, so the bundler must keep it. Per-component imports leave it free to drop what the app never names.

24 delivered files look like a webpack or CommonJS bundle. Their internal structure is not derivable from the artefact, so each counts as one file and the chunk figures below say nothing about what is inside them.
Every delivered file in js carries a source map, so every byte can be charged to the package and the module it came from.
